ideas.title: Medical debt hit 1 in 4 Americans last year, insured included, just as open enrollment opens
ideas.angle: Having insurance no longer protects people from medical debt. Several new datasets landed in the same week, and the piece would show what that debt does to health decisions: delayed care, skipped prescriptions, deductible math. It should be framed as a patient-facing guide heading into enrollment season, not a policy wonk piece.
ideas.why_now: KFF, Commonwealth Fund and Peterson-KFF data plus NYT and NPR coverage all landed this week. 'Health insurance' searches have been rising for weeks, and open enrollment season gives the story a clock.
ideas.is_it_real: Solid. Multiple independent research organizations reached the same finding, and the fact check marked it accurate. The '1 in 4' figure comes via Ohio Capital Journal's reading of the study; cite the primary Commonwealth Fund/KFF report directly. The 'health insurance' search term is generic, so treat it as supporting signal only.

ideas.title: The DRC Ebola outbreak passes 10,000 cases: what that milestone means, and where the vaccine trial stands
ideas.angle: A short, sharp item: the size of this outbreak in context, what the newly launched WHO vaccine trial can and can't do at this scale, and an honest answer on US risk.
ideas.why_now: The case count reportedly crossed 10,000 days after WHO announced a vaccine trial in DRC, and 'ebola' is rising in general search today.
ideas.is_it_real: The vaccine trial start is reported by Al Jazeera. The 10,000 figure comes from secondary aggregation and is flagged for verification; confirm it against the latest WHO situation report before writing. Big outlets have staff on this, so it fits the roundup better than a pitch.

notes: Most of today's list was sports, obituaries and celebrity noise. The fitness radar keeps catching political 'running for' queries, so its keyword matching likely needs a fix. Three keepers: the fruit cocktail lead recall folds into the existing food recall roundup, the medical-debt convergence is the strongest pitch, and Ebola goes to the roundup pending WHO confirmation of the 10K count. The bariatric durability study is on-lane but rests on one press release with significant fact-check issues, so it was dropped. If a second outlet corroborates it, it would make a good surgery-vs-GLP-1 pitch. Gym closures and fiber searches are on watch.
